slides.title: Photonic multigrid for Poisson problems
slides.source: Project implementation inspired by Lee et al. (2025)
slides.notes: 20-minute technical discussion. The contribution is a working numerical emulation and an inspectable architecture demonstrator. No experimental photonic processor or measured hardware speedup is claimed. Primary paper: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.01005.
text: Project implementation inspired by Lee et al. (2025)

A digital iterative solver with
photonic matrix–vector products
Fixed matrices and changing correction vectors solve Ax = b

slides.title: The paper assigns smoothing products to optics
slides.notes: Lee combines multigrid preconditioning with digital Krylov iteration and residual correction. The demonstrated Poisson case uses two AMG levels. Its optical core stores weights and computes smoothing products. We adopt that computational partition. Source: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.01005. The deck explains repository code rather than copying the paper figures.
text: The paper assigns smoothing products to optics
Research question: can approximate smoothing reduce digital work while reliable residuals retain accuracy?

slides.title: The residual becomes the next correction problem
slides.source: web/index.html: PhotonicSolver numerical core and embedded sparse matrix data; Lee Methods p. 16
slides.notes: Let x* denote the exact discrete solution. Then A(x*−x)=b−Ax. We can measure r without knowing x*. PCG approximately solves for δ. Corrections change only interior values; boundary changes are zero. A small true residual certifies equations are closely satisfied, not by itself a universal solution-error bound.

slides.title: The CPU closes every optical smoothing loop
slides.source: web/index.html: PhotonicSolver numerical core and embedded sparse matrix data; web/README.md hardware mapping
slides.notes: Functional hardware proposal for the browser. The CPU selects a level, retains e and g, and sends only e through shared DAC/modulator. Source illumination is not an extra numerical operation. Optical matrix weights act on the signed numerical representation; no specific signed encoding, sparse tiling, or physical switch is specified. Detector/ADC returns y, then CPU applies the Richardson update. CPU-only work does not require an extra trip through optics.

slides.title: The multigrid V-cycle
slides.source: web/index.html: PhotonicSolver numerical core and embedded sparse matrix data
slides.notes: Actual browser schedule, 3 pre and3 post sweeps at each noncoarsest level. On entry initialize e_l=0. After pre-smoothing compute d_l=g_l−A_l e_l digitally, restrict g_next=R_l d_l, recurse. On return add P_l e_next to retained e_l and post-smooth. At the top return z=e0. AMG levels are algebraic spaces, not uniformly subsampled physical meshes. In main.py the hybrid schedule is a different two-level4/0 cycle.

slides.notes: The fixed RHS r is the outer residual for this PCG call. δ starts at zero. s is the residual of this correction problem. z is one V-cycle result. q=A0p is a high-precision CPU MVM, not the optical smoothing MVM. slides.title: PCG stopping and direction updates
slides.source: web/index.html: PhotonicSolver numerical core and embedded sparse matrix data; browser inner limit: 20 iterations
slides.notes: Browser exact branch order: after δ and s updates compute ||s||/||r||. If below1e-2 returnδ. Otherwise compute another V-cycle, beta and direction update even on the final capped iteration, then the loop exits after20. The appendix records this detail. main.py instead calls SciPy CG with maxiter5 and rtol1e-12. Numerical breakdown is distinct from convergence.

slides.title: Outer correction and true-residual checks
slides.source: web/index.html: PhotonicSolver numerical core and embedded sparse matrix data; main.py solve_with_restarts

Breakdown is a separate failure state. Fresh outer r is not a recycled inner residual. This is how correction quality is checked despite approximate inner products.

slides.title: Implemented behavior and open questions
slides.source: main.py: original solver, observed by presentation/build/collect_python.py; web/README.md; Lee Methods
slides.notes: Paper-inspired structure is implemented, not an exact hardware reproduction. main.py quantizes the input and adds fresh Gaussian output noise. It has no matrix quantization, physical encoding, averaging or timing. Browser uses ideal MVMs and a functional shared-converter diagram. Classical PCG assumptions are not guaranteed under noisy variable asymmetric preconditioning. Zhu related work supports coherent signed multiplication with digital memory/reconfiguration, not a claimed replacement for the current multigrid code. References: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.01005; https://doi.org/10.1021/acsphotonics.3c01694.

slides.title: Recursive V-cycle and smoothing pseudocode
slides.source: web/index.html: PhotonicSolver numerical core and embedded sparse matrix data
slides.notes: V(l,g) returns a local correction. R_l=P_l transpose. The coarse solve uses elimination, not an explicit inverse. CPU computes d and all transfer products. e starts at zero only on V-cycle entry; post-smoothing starts from the corrected value. Main2D cycle differs and is shown later.
text: Every operation belongs to a CPU or optical assignment
Appendix  ·  web/index.html: PhotonicSolver numerical core and embedded sparse matrix data

V(l, g):
  if l = 3: return solve(A₃, g)
  e = 0
  repeat 3 times: e = Smooth(l, e, g)
  d = g − Aℓe                 [CPU]
  gc = Rℓd                    [CPU]
  ec = V(l + 1, gc)
  e = e + Pℓec                [CPU]
  repeat 3 times: e = Smooth(l, e, g)
  return e

Smooth(l, e, g):

encode e
y = Aℓe      [optical]
detect y
e = e + ωℓ(g − y)
                 [CPU]
return e
At level 0, g₀ = s and V(0, s) returns z. The outer solution x is separate.

slides.title: Convergence theory and observed results
slides.source: SciPy CG documentation; main.py; web/index.html
slides.notes: SciPy CG requires Hermitian positive definiteA and a Hermitian positive definite preconditioner. The standard fixed linear SPD-preconditioner argument doesnot transfer automatically to this noisy, quantized, asymmetric action. This run converges empirically. A nextcomparison should include flexibleKrylov formulations and multiple noise realizations. https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.sparse.linalg.cg.html . Residual-error relation is exact for invertibleA; conditioning and discretization remain distinct.
